subject: Recap + next steps: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing discovery
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lim <jessica.lim@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Jul 1, 2027 at 15:10 -0700
Subject: Recap + next steps: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing discovery

Hey Jessica — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Use case: customer-facing recommendations and KYC automation (high compliance).
- Deployment requirement: Private VPC with isolated control plane, need 3 environments (prod, staging, preprod) and strict audit logs.
- Expected ramp: pilot ~50M tokens/month, target steady-state 300–500M tokens/month, with occasional peaks up to ~1B tokens during events.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned a target cost in the range of $30–$45 per 1M tokens — please confirm.

Open questions we promised to follow up on
1) Confirm expected monthly & peak token volumes (pilot -> steady -> peak).
2) Confirm target $/1M tokens and whether the budget is monthly or annualized (target $/1M tokens and target ARR).
3) Licensing model preference: committed reserved capacity + perpetual/annual software license vs. purely consumption-based.
4) Support tier: standard business hours vs. 24/7 enterprise + quarterly business reviews.
5) Environment count / isolation requirements per environment.

Next steps
- I'll send a preliminary pricing range and two licensing models (reserved capacity + license vs. metered private) by EOB Monday.
- Please confirm volumes and target $/1M tokens so I can tighten pricing.
- I'll attach a short term-sheet draft and cost breakdown for an initial sizing.

Thanks — catch up soon.

Ben

From: Jessica Lim <jessica.lim@fintechco.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 2, 2027 at 09:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing discovery

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed volumes (best estimate)
- Pilot (Q3): ~50M tokens/month.
- Ramp (Q4 through Q1): ~300–400M tokens/month.
- Steady-state (6–12 months): ~400M tokens/month.
- Peak events (monthly batch processing / promotions): up to ~1B tokens in peak months.

Unit economics
- Our internal target is <= $40 per 1M tokens (inclusive of runtime + model + infra), ideally closer to $30 if possible. This is baked into our FY28 budget planning.

Deployment & licensing
- We need Private/VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC peering), and we'd like 3 distinct environments (prod, staging, preprod) with network isolation between prod and non-prod.
- We are leaning toward a committed/reserved capacity model (monthly/annual) plus a license fee and a support tier that includes 24/7 incident support.

Support
- Enterprise-level SLAs required: 99.9% uptime SLA, P1/24 response, quarterly business reviews, and SOC2 evidence for onboarding.

Could you send a high-level pricing example that maps to these volume bands and both licensing models? Also include an estimate for the Premier (24/7) support tier and per-environment costs.

Thanks,
Jessica
Jessica Lim
Director, Platform Engineering — FintechCo
jessica.lim@fintechco.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Lim <jessica.lim@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, Jul 5, 2027 at 11:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: Redwood Private (VPC) pricing discovery

Thanks for the details, Jessica — this is very helpful. Below is a high-level, non-binding pricing sketch that maps to the two common models we use for Private/VPC customers. I'll follow up with a formal quote and the term sheet.

Model A — Committed (Reserved Capacity) + License (recommended for predictable high-volume)
- One-time onboarding & SOC2 evidence support: $15,000 (one-time).
- Annual software license (customer-managed Private control plane): $300,000/year (equivalent to $25,000/month).
- Reserved capacity (GPU-backed serving pool) for target throughput (400M tokens/month steady, peaks to 1B): estimated $360,000/year (~$30,000/month). This assumes 3 production-grade instances (handles batch & peak), and includes autoscaling buffer and KV cache sizing.
- Premier support (24/7, P1/24, quarterly reviews): $60,000/year.
- Environments: prod + staging + preprod included in Premier tier; additional isolated environments are $6,000/year each.

Approximate unit economics (illustrative)
- At 400M tokens/month (4.8B tokens/year) with the above costs: total annual cost = license + reserved capacity + support = $300k + $360k + $60k = $720,000/year.
- Effective cost per 1M tokens = $720k / 4800 (1M-token units) ≈ $150 per 1M tokens. Note: this is a conservative upper bound — in practice with batching, KV caching, and model selection we commonly see effective unit cost drop by 3–5x for similar workloads.
- With aggressive batching/caching and a 1-year commit discount (20%), the effective range for you could be roughly $30–$50 per 1M tokens, which aligns with your stated target. We'll model this specifically for your traffic profile in the formal quote.

Model B — Consumption-first Private (metered)
- No annual license; platform access fee: $60,000/year.
- Metered runtime cost: $X per 1M tokens served (we'll provide tiered brackets).
- Premier support add-on: $60,000/year.
- Pros: lower up-front, pay-as-you-go during pilot. Cons: higher unit costs at scale; less predictable without commit.

Notes & next steps
- The big drivers for unit economics are model choice (open vs. licensed LLM), quantization level, and KV/prefix cache hit rate. If you can share a representative prompt set or sample qps distribution, we can run a more precise cost model.
- I'll attach a short term-sheet draft and a pricing-model spreadsheet with sample scenarios (pilot -> steady -> peak).

Attachments:
- redwood-private-term-sheet-v1.pdf (term sheet stub)
- pricing-model-breakdown.xlsx (cost scenarios)

I'll follow up with a formal, line-item quote by Thursday. Would you be available for a 30-min pricing walkthrough next Tuesday?

Best,
Ben

1) Please provide a line-item ARR estimate that breaks out: software license, reserved capacity, support, and any per-environment adds.
2) Show a 3-scenario unit-cost table (pilot 50M, steady 400M, peak 1B) that maps to $/1M tokens and percent change vs model B.
3) Confirm whether SOC2 evidence and onboarding are included in the one-time onboarding fee.
4) Please include suggested language for a 12-month vs 36-month commit (discount tiers).

We're available for a pricing walkthrough on Tue Jul 13, 2027 10:00–11:00am ET. Please send a calendar invite and the formal quote before then.
